commit 2c98be45ad9b2a49ceac4b6ab73fd7d715168775
feat: add ppc64le builds using the wasmi interpreter backend

Neither Cranelift nor wasmer's LLVM backend can generate powerpc64 code,
so plugins are run through wasmer's pure-Rust wasmi interpreter on that
architecture. Unlike loongarch64, this needs no prebuilt LLVM cross image.

The backend is selected by a `wasm_interpreter` cfg (set for target_arch
= "powerpc64", or via the new `wasm-interpreter` feature for testing on
other architectures). On that path the plugin cache stores raw wasm bytes
instead of a serialized native artifact.

Issue #1024

commit 52a73beb6323ac74176aecbb6e3e639256955dc1
fix(ci): build powerpc64le musl via docker run instead of cross

cross runs the container as the non-root host user, but the
rust-musl-cross image keeps its rustup at root-owned /root/.rustup, so
installing the pinned toolchain failed with "Permission denied". Build
that target with a direct `docker run` (as root, the image's intended
usage) and chown the output back to the runner afterward.

wasmer-compiler pulls in wasmer-vm -> corosensei, whose powerpc64 inline
asm requires nightly and doesn't build on stable. The interpreter build
doesn't need a compiler backend, so depend on wasmer-compiler only off
powerpc64 and use a stable literal for the wasm cache version there.
